title: What did the search miss?
hook: A small search is only part of the landscape.

knows: A sample examines part of a larger area.
doesNotKnow: A sample with no finds need not imply that unsearched locations have none.

misconception: No finds in the sample prove none exist elsewhere.
objective: Distinguish a sample result from a statement about every patch.

claims.text: In a constructed set of ten patches, the first three sampled patches have no fossil, while the sixth patch has one. A sample without finds does not prove all unsearched locations lack fossils.
claims.source: Arithmetic and declared constructed example; not field data.

claims.text: The stage is a schematic model, with stated example values or sample counts; it is not a reconstruction of an observed field site.
Recall: A researcher inspects two of ten boxes and sees no shells. What follows? The observation applies to the checked boxes; it does not determine the contents of the rest.
claims.source: Relative order or arithmetic under the explicitly stated example conditions.

recall.question: A researcher inspects two of ten boxes and sees no shells. What follows?
options: The two checked boxes have no observed shells
All ten boxes contain no shells
recall.why: The observation applies to the checked boxes; it does not determine the contents of the rest.
